articles.title: Cold one day, 37°C heat the next: Karnataka faces unusual weather, health alert - NewsFirst Prime
articles.full_text:
From chilly mornings to sweating afternoons, Karnataka is witnessing sharp weather changes and temperatures touching 37°C even during the monsoon. The rising heat has put the health department on alert over a possible increase in infectious diseases.
Karnataka is witnessing unusual weather conditions, with temperatures rising even during the monsoon season and sharp changes being seen from one day to another.
While one day may bring chilly weather, the next can see strong heat and sweating. Temperatures have touched 37°C in parts of the state despite the ongoing monsoon, raising concerns about the possible impact of the changing weather on public health.
The changing conditions have been linked to the global ‘Super El Nino’ effect, with concerns that temperatures could rise further in the coming days.
The state is also facing the possibility of recording unusually high temperatures, with the current trend raising concerns about a record rise in temperature over a three-year period.

The health impact of such sudden weather changes is now a major concern. The changing temperature and weather conditions could create favourable conditions for the spread of infectious diseases, prompting the Health Department to step up its preparedness.
The department is taking precautionary measures to ensure that the health system is ready if cases of infectious diseases increase.
Hospitals asked to stay prepared
The Health Department has directed government hospitals across the state to maintain adequate stocks of essential life-saving medicines.
Hospitals have also been asked to keep ORS packets, testing kits and sufficient beds ready so that patients can receive timely treatment if the health situation worsens.
The preparations are being carried out under the guidance of the Health Minister, with instructions aimed at preventing a possible health crisis linked to the changing weather conditions.
Dengue, chikungunya testing strengthened
Laboratory preparedness is another major part of the state's response.
Government laboratories are being readied for the testing of dengue and chikungunya, two infectious diseases that require early detection and timely treatment.
The focus is on ensuring that suspected cases can be tested without delay and that the health system can respond quickly if infections begin to rise.

ASHA workers to monitor symptoms
The Health Department is also strengthening surveillance at the field level.
ASHA workers and other health personnel have been instructed to conduct door-to-door surveys to identify symptoms at an early stage.
The aim is to detect possible infections quickly instead of waiting for cases to become serious. Early identification will help health officials monitor the situation and take necessary action in affected areas.
High-level meeting planned
Officials are also closely watching the weather situation in Bengaluru and other parts of Karnataka.
Considering the changing weather pattern and the possibility of further temperature increases, preparations are being made for a high-level meeting to discuss the next course of action.
The government is expected to review the weather situation and the health risks associated with it, while deciding further preventive measures.
With temperatures rising, sudden shifts between cold and heat becoming noticeable and the possibility of further warming remaining a concern, the Health Department is preparing hospitals, laboratories and field-level health workers to respond to any increase in infectious diseases.
